- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off sentiment.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points), especially in early forecast window; apply dampening factor for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10+ consecutive days show price moving away from 65–75 range, model tends to overreact; cap forecast near historical mean (65–75) for 3–7 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often misses late-term corrections (last 5–7 days); add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative or price shows divergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lead time adjustment for sentiment shifts.
